finding.claim: Any authenticated user can delete any project because the ownership/admin check's return value is discarded.
finding.source: The :id path parameter (req.params.id) on an authenticated DELETE /projects/:id request, plus the attacker's own session (req.user). Precondition: the attacker is logged in and does not own the target project.
finding.sink: api.js:19 req.store.projects.delete(project.id), a destructive state change on a project the attacker does not own.

trace.note: router.delete('/projects/:id') accepts any authenticated request; no middleware-level check is visible in this file.
project = req.store.projects.get(req.params.id) loads the target by id with no owner scope.
authorized(req.user, project) is called as a bare statement. It returns true/false and never throws, so its result is ignored.
Responds 204, so the deletion succeeds silently.

finding.guards_checked: (1) authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and does not throw, and its result is not read at line 18, so it cannot gate the action. (2) The predicate itself (ownerId === user.id || isAdmin === true) is correct in isolation. (3) If the project is missing, line 18 throws a TypeError (500) before the delete, so that case is not exploitable. (4) The PUT handler at api.js:25 uses the throwing authorize() and is enforced correctly; the DELETE handler is the inconsistent one. Not verified: whether upstream middleware restricts DELETE to owners/admins, and how req.store is scoped per tenant, since neither is in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so its result is discarded and it gates nothing; no other guard exists in api.js (the only other file in the directory is none, so no upstream middleware is visible). The throwing authorize() at api.js:4-10 is used only by the PUT handler at api.js:25, not the DELETE handler.
verdict.reason: The DELETE handler at api.js:16-20 calls req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19 unconditionally after a discarded boolean check at api.js:18, so any authenticated user who knows a project id can delete it; the only remaining uncertainty is whether unseen upstream middleware restricts DELETE, which is not in this directory.
